passages.text: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus.
They came to Him at that time.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ προσῆλθον οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντες Τίς ἄρα μείζων ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: Jesus invited a little child to stand among them.
passages.sermon: Jesus called a little child.\r\nHe brought the child to stand in the middle of the disciples.\r\nThe child stood among them.
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος παιδίον ἔστησεν αὐτὸ ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν

passages.text: “Truly I tell you,” He said, “unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “I tell you the truth.”
You must change your ways.
You must become like little children.
If you do not become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ στραφῆτε καὶ γένησθε ὡς τὰ παιδία οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He pointed to a little child standing among them.
He said, “Whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.”
A person must become humble like a child.
This humble person is the greatest in God’s kingdom.
passages.original: ὅστις οὖν ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὡς τὸ παιδίον τοῦτο οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ μείζων ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν

passages.text: And whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He taught them about the kingdom of heaven.
He said, “Whoever welcomes a little child like this in My name welcomes Me.”
If you receive a child because of Jesus, you receive Jesus Himself.
Welcoming a child in Jesus’ name is the same as welcoming Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ὃς ἐὰν δέξηται ἓν παιδίον τοιοῦτο ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματί μου ἐμὲ δέχεται

passages.text: But if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about those who believe in Him.
Some of these believers are little ones.
If anyone causes one of these little ones to stumble, that person does great harm.
It would be better for that person to have a large millstone hung around his neck.
It would be better for him to be drowned in the depths of the sea.
passages.original: Ὃς δ’ ἂν σκανδαλίσῃ ἕνα τῶν μικρῶν τούτων τῶν πιστευόντων εἰς ἐμέ συμφέρει αὐτῷ ἵνα κρεμασθῇ μύλος ὀνικὸς περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ καταποντισθῇ ἐν τῷ πελάγει τῆς θαλάσσης

passages.text: Woe to the world for the causes of sin. These stumbling blocks must come, but woe to the man through whom they come!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about sin and its causes.
He said, “Woe to the world because of the things that cause people to sin.”
Sinful things will happen in the world.
These stumbling blocks must come.
But woe to the person who brings sin to others.
God will judge the one who causes others to sin.
passages.original: Οὐαὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἀπὸ τῶν σκανδάλων ἀνάγκη γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τὰ σκάνδαλα πλὴν οὐαὶ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ δι’ οὗ τὸ σκάνδαλον ἔρχεται

passages.text: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to His disciples.
Jesus warns about sin.
If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off.
If your foot causes you to sin, cut it off.
Throw it away from you.
It is better for you to enter life crippled or lame.
It is better to have only one hand or one foot and enter life.
It is worse to have two hands and two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
passages.original: Εἰ δὲ ἡ χείρ σου ἢ ὁ πούς σου σκανδαλίζει σε ἔκκοψον αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ καλόν σοί ἐστιν εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν ζωὴν κυλλὸν ἢ χωλόν ἢ δύο χεῖρας ἢ δύο πόδας ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον

passages.text: And if your eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away. It is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
passages.sermon:
Jesus warns about sin and its dangers.
If your eye causes you to sin, remove it.
Throw it away from you.
It is better for you to enter life with one eye.
It is worse to have two eyes and be thrown into the fire of hell.
passages.original: καὶ εἰ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου σκανδαλίζει σε ἔξελε αὐτὸν καὶ βάλε ἀπὸ σοῦ καλόν σοί ἐστιν μονόφθαλμον εἰς τὴν ζωὴν εἰσελθεῖν ἢ δύο ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντα βληθῆναι εἰς τὴν γέενναν τοῦ πυρός

passages.text: See that you do not look down on any of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always see the face of My Father in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about their attitude toward others.
He said, “Do not look down on any of these little ones.”
These little ones are people who seem unimportant or weak.
Jesus explained why they matter.
He said, “Their angels are in heaven.”
These angels always see the face of My Father in heaven.
God the Father is in heaven.
The angels of these little ones are always before God.
God cares about every little one.
passages.original: Ὁρᾶτε μὴ καταφρονήσητε ἑνὸς τῶν μικρῶν τούτων λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτῶν ἐν οὐρανοῖς διὰ παντὸς βλέπουσι τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the hills and go out to search for the one that is lost?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He used a story about a shepherd.
A shepherd has one hundred sheep.
One sheep goes astray.
The shepherd leaves the ninety-nine sheep on the hills.
He goes out to search for the one lost sheep.
passages.original: Τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ ἐὰν γένηταί τινι ἀνθρώπῳ ἑκατὸν πρόβατα καὶ πλανηθῇ ἓν ἐξ αὐτῶν οὐχὶ ἀφήσει τὰ ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα ἐπὶ τὰ ὄρη καὶ πορευθεὶς ζητεῖ τὸ πλανώμενον

passages.text: And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices more over that one sheep than over the ninety-nine that did not go astray.
passages.sermon:
A man has one hundred sheep.
One sheep goes astray.
The man searches for the lost sheep.
If the man finds the lost sheep, he rejoices.
He rejoices more over the one sheep he found than over the ninety-nine sheep that did not go astray.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν γένηται εὑρεῖν αὐτό ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι χαίρει ἐπ’ αὐτῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἐπὶ τοῖς ἐνενήκοντα ἐννέα τοῖς μὴ πεπλανημένοις

passages.text: In the same way, your Father in heaven is not willing that any of these little ones should perish.
passages.sermon:
God is your Father.
God lives in heaven.
God does not want any of these little ones to be lost.
God does not want even one of them to perish.
passages.original: οὕτως οὐκ ἔστιν θέλημα ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Πατρὸς ὑμῶν τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἵνα ἀπόληται ἓν τῶν μικρῶν τούτων

passages.text: If your brother sins against you, go and confront him privately. If he listens to you, you have won your brother over.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches about forgiveness and reconciliation among believers.
If your brother sins against you, act.
Go to your brother.
Speak to him alone.
Tell him his fault.
If he listens to you, you have won your brother back.
passages.original: Ἐὰν δὲ ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ὕπαγε ἔλεγξον αὐτὸν μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου ἐάν σου ἀκούσῃ ἐκέρδησας τὸν ἀδελφόν σου

passages.text: But if he will not listen, take one or two others along, so that ‘every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.’
passages.sermon:
If your brother does not listen to you, do not go alone again.
Take one or two other people with you.
These people will be witnesses.
Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
This is how you confirm what happened.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀκούσῃ παράλαβε μετὰ σοῦ ἔτι ἕνα ἢ δύο ἵνα Ἐπὶ στόματος δύο μαρτύρων ἢ τριῶν σταθῇ πᾶν ῥῆμα

passages.text: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, regard him as you would a pagan or a tax collector.
passages.sermon:
Jesus teaches about dealing with a brother who sins against you.
If your brother does not listen to you and the witnesses, tell the church.
If your brother does not listen to the church, treat him as you would treat a pagan.
Treat him as you would treat a tax collector.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ παρακούσῃ αὐτῶν εἰπὸν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐὰν δὲ καὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας παρακούσῃ ἔστω σοι ὥσπερ ὁ ἐθνικὸς καὶ ὁ τελώνης

passages.text: Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Truly, I tell you this.”
You have authority on earth.
Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven.
Whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.
passages.original: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅσα ἐὰν δήσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται δεδεμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ὅσα ἐὰν λύσητε ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἔσται λελυμένα ἐν οὐρανῷ

passages.text: Again, I tell you truly that if two of you on the earth agree about anything you ask for, it will be done for you by My Father in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
If two of you agree on earth about anything you ask for,
My Father in heaven will do it for you.”
passages.original: Πάλιν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἐὰν δύο συμφωνήσωσιν ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς περὶ παντὸς πράγματος οὗ ἐὰν αἰτήσωνται γενήσεται αὐτοῖς παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: For where two or three gather together in My name, there am I with them.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
When two people gather in the name of Jesus, He is present with them.
When three people gather in the name of Jesus, He is present with them.
Jesus is with every group that gathers in His name.
passages.original: οὗ γάρ εἰσιν δύο ἢ τρεῖς συνηγμένοι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα ἐκεῖ εἰμι ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν

passages.text: Then Peter came to Jesus and asked, “Lord, how many times shall I forgive my brother who sins against me? Up to seven times?”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter came to Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter asked Jesus a question.
Peter said, “Lord, my brother may sin against me.”
Peter asked, “How many times should I forgive my brother?”
Peter suggested a number.
Peter asked, “Should I forgive him up to seven times?”
passages.original: Τότε προσελθὼν ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Κύριε ποσάκις ἁμαρτήσει εἰς ἐμὲ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀφήσω αὐτῷ ἕως ἑπτάκις

passages.text: Jesus answered, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Peter asked about forgiveness.
Peter wanted to know how many times to forgive a brother who sins.
Peter suggested forgiving up to seven times.
Jesus answered Peter directly.
Jesus said, "Do not forgive only seven times."
Jesus said, "Forgive seventy-seven times."
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐ λέγω σοι ἕως ἑπτάκις ἀλλὰ ἕως ἑβδομηκοντάκις ἑπτά

passages.text: Because of this, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus explained forgiveness.
Jesus said the kingdom of heaven is like a king.
This king wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ βασιλεῖ ὃς ἠθέλησεν συνᾶραι λόγον μετὰ τῶν δούλων αὐτοῦ

passages.text: As he began the settlements, a debtor was brought to him owing ten thousand talents.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a story about the kingdom of heaven.
A king wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
The king began the settlements.
Someone brought a debtor to the king.
This debtor owed the king ten thousand talents.
passages.original: ἀρξαμένου δὲ αὐτοῦ συναίρειν προσηνέχθη εἷς αὐτῷ ὀφειλέτης μυρίων ταλάντων

passages.text: Since the man was unable to pay, the master ordered that he be sold to pay his debt, along with his wife and children and everything he owned.
passages.sermon:
A king wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
One servant owed the king a great debt.
This servant could not pay the debt.
The king gave an order.
He ordered that the servant be sold.
He ordered that the servant’s wife be sold.
He ordered that the servant’s children be sold.
He ordered that everything the servant owned be sold.
The king wanted payment for the debt.
passages.original: μὴ ἔχοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀποδοῦναι ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος πραθῆναι καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀποδοθῆναι

passages.text: Then the servant fell on his knees before him. ‘Have patience with me,’ he begged, ‘and I will pay back everything.’
passages.sermon:
A servant owed his master a great debt.
The master ordered the servant to be sold because he could not pay.
The servant fell on his knees before the master.
He begged the master for patience.
He said, “Have patience with me.”
He promised, “I will pay back everything.”
passages.original: Πεσὼν οὖν ὁ δοῦλος προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί καὶ πάντα ἀποδώσω σοι

passages.text: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt, and released him.
passages.sermon:
The master saw the servant’s situation.
The master felt compassion for the servant.
The master forgave the servant’s debt.
The master released the servant.
passages.original: Σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος τοῦ δούλου ἐκείνου ἀπέλυσεν αὐτόν καὶ τὸ δάνειον ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ

passages.text: But when that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii. He grabbed him and began to choke him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe me!’
passages.sermon:
The servant had just been forgiven a great debt by his master.
He went out.
He found one of his fellow servants.
This fellow servant owed him one hundred denarii.
He seized his fellow servant.
He began to choke him.
He said, "Pay back what you owe me."
passages.original: Ἐξελθὼν δὲ ὁ δοῦλος ἐκεῖνος εὗρεν ἕνα τῶν συνδούλων αὐτοῦ ὃς ὤφειλεν αὐτῷ ἑκατὸν δηνάρια καὶ κρατήσας αὐτὸν ἔπνιγεν λέγων Ἀπόδος εἴ τι ὀφείλεις

passages.text: So his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.’
passages.sermon:
A fellow servant owed the first servant money.
This fellow servant fell down before the first servant.
He begged the first servant.
He said, “Have patience with me.”
He said, “I will pay you back.”
passages.original: Πεσὼν οὖν ὁ σύνδουλος αὐτοῦ παρεκάλει αὐτὸν λέγων Μακροθύμησον ἐπ’ ἐμοί καὶ ἀποδώσω σοι

passages.text: But he refused. Instead, he went and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay his debt.
passages.sermon:
The servant refused to show mercy.
He did not forgive his fellow servant.
He went away.
He had his fellow servant thrown into prison.
He demanded that the debt be paid in full.
He kept his fellow servant in prison until the debt was paid.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτὸν εἰς φυλακὴν ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ τὸ ὀφειλόμενον

passages.text: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were greatly distressed, and they went and recounted all of this to their master.
passages.sermon:
The fellow servants saw what happened.
They felt very sad.
They went to their master.
They told their master everything that had happened.
passages.original: Ἰδόντες οὖν οἱ σύνδουλοι αὐτοῦ τὰ γενόμενα ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα καὶ ἐλθόντες διεσάφησαν τῷ κυρίῳ ἑαυτῶν πάντα τὰ γενόμενα

passages.text: Then the master summoned him and declared, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.
passages.sermon:
The master called the servant to him.
The master spoke to the servant.
The master said, "You are a wicked servant."
I forgave all your debt.
You begged me to forgive you.
I forgave you because you asked me.
passages.original: Τότε προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ λέγει αὐτῷ Δοῦλε πονηρέ πᾶσαν τὴν ὀφειλὴν ἐκείνην ἀφῆκά σοι ἐπεὶ παρεκάλεσάς με

passages.text: Shouldn’t you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?’
passages.sermon:
The master spoke to the servant.
The master had forgiven the servant’s great debt.
The master had shown mercy to the servant.
The servant had begged for this mercy.
The master asked the servant a question.
The master said, “You should have shown mercy to your fellow servant.
I showed mercy to you.
You should have done the same for him.”
passages.original: οὐκ ἔδει καὶ σὲ ἐλεῆσαι τὸν σύνδουλόν σου ὡς κἀγὼ σὲ ἠλέησα

passages.text: In anger his master turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he should repay all that he owed.
passages.sermon:
The master became angry.
The master had a servant who owed him a debt.
The master handed the servant over to the jailers.
The jailers would torture the servant.
The servant would remain with the jailers until he repaid everything he owed.
passages.original: καὶ ὀργισθεὶς ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν τοῖς βασανισταῖς ἕως οὗ ἀποδῷ πᾶν τὸ ὀφειλόμενον αὐτῷ

passages.text: That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your heart.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus taught about forgiveness.
God is the heavenly Father.
God will act toward you as the master acted in the story.
God will do this if you do not forgive others.
You must forgive your brother.
You must forgive from your heart.
If you do not forgive, God will not forgive you.
passages.original: Οὕτως καὶ ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ποιήσει ὑμῖν ἐὰν μὴ ἀφῆτε ἕκαστος τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν καρδιῶν ὑμῶν
